principles.text: Concerned this could be the start of a bear market given very poor breadth, extended prior moves and no real correction in 3-4 years; compares it to the 2021-22 stage-3 to stage-4 transition.
When the indices are extended from the 9 EMA, wait for a pullback to the hourly 9 EMA, or the next day / daily 9 EMA, before shorting; shorting too early into extension was a mistake.
Does not want to chase or short into weakness after missing an entry; waits for a bounce instead.
Flags his own risk of overtrading on a day with no clear opportunity.

Studies charts by zooming out on weekly/daily to find explosive moves (big % in 1-3 weeks or a month) or long-lasting trends (6+ months), both up and down; studies intraday entries on lower timeframes via replay, with a smaller sample.
Started by going through every Nasdaq-100 and S&P stock one by one, focused on explosive/long-lasting move periods; now also studies past moves of stocks he recently traded.
Avoids trading chat rooms: too much noise from inexperienced traders, conflicting opinions; trading is personal and better studied alone unless you find a genuinely good partner.
On a day he judges unfavourable for his side, he tightens the stop tighter than the natural level (e.g. inside the daily VWAP) to limit loss.
Will take a setup he likes on a poor day only with an extremely tight stop and tiny risk (~0.02% per trade, well under 0.1%); a stop-out is a small 'donation', a winner is a killer trade.
After a huge breakdown candle, a quick snapback the next day or day after into the declining daily 9 EMA is shortable; better entries are above the 9 or at the 21 EMA.
If the day looks too strong, wait for the next day or for a higher level (21 EMA, or 50 EMA on the hourly) to short.
Shorting UVXY even after a parabolic run is too dangerous (it can run another 30%+, 1,000% in 2020); going long the Qs or stocks is preferable.
Trades leveraged ETFs based on analysis of the underlying but sets the stop on the leveraged ETF itself, accepting occasional stop-outs the underlying would not have hit.
Does not move stops after entering a trade; fears it would become a bad habit.
Agrees that the higher the timeframe, the stronger an EMA acts as support/resistance.
Not attracted to longs while the market does not favour the long side; wants more confirmation and wider participation across sectors and stock types before going long.
Does not take partial profits when a tight-stop trade moves fast in his favour; a fast move is a sign to hold for a multi-day or multi-week swing.
After a strong month he sizes up much slower than account growth, to control drawdown and prevent oversizing; today's shorts in total were under 20% sizing.
After a good period he notices he becomes less patient and does not wait for the best opportunities; smaller sizing limits the damage.
Gap risk on shorts was higher than usual; if no strong close, he may reduce exposure before the close.
He only stays up for the US close when volatility is high and he has heavy exposure or margin; high leverage costs sleep and lifestyle, and he will increasingly prioritise health over performance.
Takes trades mostly near the open, sometimes midday, very rarely near the close.
Probably would take less risk after hitting a large account milestone.
Will still short even if the intraday chart makes higher highs and higher lows, if price is moving into resistance (e.g. the daily 9 EMA) and shows rejection/distribution selling.

Holds a sector ETF (SOXL) through component earnings: with profit cushion, the ETF reduces single-stock risk, and in earnings season you cannot avoid all reports, so some uncertainty must be accepted.

Intraday short triggers are flexible: 5-minute 9 EMA / candle breakdown with stop at the breakdown candle high, a 1-minute breakdown if price gets higher into the 50 EMA, or an anchored-VWAP rejection from the high of day; shorting breakdowns or bounces both work.
Traders using wider 2-4% stops can use 15-minute candle breakdowns; higher timeframe triggers give less noise and fewer losing trades.
With volatility ahead, shorts are taken without crazy sizing and with preparation for gap ups.

When anchored VWAP differs by timeframe he treats it as a range, with the daily level most important; may take a first try at the hourly AVWAP and, if it fails, retry near the daily level once it shows rejection or an intraday breakout.
Anchors VWAP only at swing highs/lows, earnings, IPO day, or huge gap ups/downs.
Prefers price to have shown respect/reaction at an anchored VWAP before taking the trade, though not mandatory.
For shorts he tends to cover into weakness (gap downs, previous swing lows) rather than wait for a close and trail with the 9/21 EMA; on longs he sells into gap ups.
